events.title: Viking raiders plunder Paris and hold it for ransom
events.description: A Viking fleet of 120 ships under the Norse chieftain Reginherus, or Ragnar, sailed up the Seine and plundered and occupied Paris, holding it for a large ransom. Reginherus has been tentatively identified with the legendary Ragnar Lodbrok.

events.title: Pope Innocent II endorses the Knights Templar in Omne datum optimum
events.description: In the papal bull Omne datum optimum, Pope Innocent II endorsed the Knights Templar, officially approving the Templar Rule and placing the order under papal protection. The order had been founded in Jerusalem to protect pilgrims.

events.title: The Ottoman Empire takes Thessaloniki from Venice after a long siege
events.description: After a siege begun in 1422, the Ottoman Empire under Sultan Murad II captured Thessaloniki from the Republic of Venice. The city remained in Ottoman hands until it became part of the Kingdom of Greece in 1912.

events.title: Yorkists win the Battle of Towton
events.description: Fought in a snowstorm on Palm Sunday in Yorkshire, Towton is often called the bloodiest battle on English soil, with traditional estimates of 28,000 dead. It secured the throne for Edward IV.
events.html: Fought in a snowstorm on Palm Sunday in Yorkshire, Towton is often called the bloodiest battle on English soil, with traditional estimates of 28,000 dead. It secured the throne for Edward IV.

events.title: Swedish settlers found New Sweden on the Delaware
events.description: Colonists from the Kalmar Nyckel and Fogel Grip landed at the site of Wilmington and built Fort Christina. The Dutch took New Sweden in 1655, but its log cabins became an American tradition.
events.html: Colonists from the Kalmar Nyckel and Fogel Grip landed at the site of Wilmington and built Fort Christina. The Dutch took New Sweden in 1655, but its log cabins became an American tradition.

events.title: Ice jam stops Niagara Falls
events.description: Ice blocking the Niagara River at Lake Erie reduced the falls to a trickle for over a day. Sightseers walked on the riverbed; it is the only time the falls are known to have stopped naturally.
events.html: Ice blocking the Niagara River at Lake Erie reduced the falls to a trickle for over a day. Sightseers walked on the riverbed; it is the only time the falls are known to have stopped naturally.

events.title: Queen Victoria signs the British North America Act
events.description: The act united the Province of Canada, Nova Scotia and New Brunswick as the Dominion of Canada. Confederation took effect on 1 July, now Canada Day.

events.title: Julius and Ethel Rosenberg convicted of espionage
events.description: A New York jury found the couple guilty of conspiring to pass atomic secrets to the Soviet Union. Their execution in 1953 remained controversial, especially over Ethel's role.

events.title: Last US combat troops leave South Vietnam
events.description: The final American combat units departed under the Paris Peace Accords, and the last prisoners of war were released. Some 58,000 Americans and millions of Vietnamese had died in the war.
